verify_method: Phase 1 live pass via Exa against primary sources; Phase 2 efficacy enrichment via Consensus. Statuses reflect what THIS pass could confirm — honest by design.

claims.claim: Landmark prevalence research on Nebraska's commercial sex market found roughly 800 individuals advertised for sex online in the state each month, with about 15% showing multiple high-risk trafficking indicators and 7 in 10 showing at least one indicator of being trafficked.
claims.source: Creighton University Human Trafficking Initiative / HTI Labs (Price & Clark), Nebraska's Commercial Sex Market (funded by Women's Fund of Omaha); reported by Nebraska Public Media, 'Sold for Sex.'
claims.expiry: Vintage-limited: rests on 2017-era Backpage data; Backpage was seized in 2018. No post-Backpage update from HTI Labs (htilabs.org) surfaced this pass.
red_team_flags: Figure varies by source: the primary Creighton/HTI reporting says ~800/month (~130/day); some secondary sources (e.g. Kulig & Butler 2019) cite ~900/month. Claim rewritten to ~800 to match the primary source.
The original '75% of those trafficked are Nebraskans' sub-claim was NOT confirmed this pass — pull it from the primary HTI report before use, or drop it.
Vintage: 2017-era Backpage data. Frame explicitly as 'landmark prevalence research,' or replace with a post-Backpage HTI Labs update before federal submission.

claims.claim: NCMEC's CyberTipline received more than 546,000 reports of online enticement in 2024 — roughly a 192% increase over 2023 and a twelve-fold increase since 2021.
claims.source: NCMEC CyberTipline 2024 Data Report; corroborated in U.S. Senate Judiciary Committee testimony (2025).
claims.expiry: NCMEC releases annual CyberTipline data each spring; refresh with the full-year 2025 report.
red_team_flags: Cross-source variance: NCMEC testimony variously cites a 192% and a 194% increase over 2023 (~186,000 reports). 'Roughly 192%' is safe.
This is reporting volume (driven partly by REPORT Act mandates), not a direct prevalence measure — say so.

efficacy_evidence.title: Building the Evidence on Preventing Youth Commercial Sexual Exploitation: Evaluation of the Not a Number Trafficking Prevention Program
efficacy_evidence.cite: Jones et al., 2025, Journal of Interpersonal Violence
efficacy_evidence.finding: Quasi-experimental evaluation found a youth trafficking-prevention education program increased CSE awareness and help-seeking self-efficacy.

claims.claim: In 2024 NCMEC received nearly 100 reports of financial sextortion per day; teenage boys are the predominant victims.
claims.source: NCMEC, 2024 in Numbers (May 2025); Thorn, Trends in Financial Sextortion (2024).
red_team_flags: The per-day rate and the male-teen skew are well corroborated (Thorn: 90% of victims with age+gender were males 14–17). However, the original 'at least 36 teenage boys have died by suicide since 2021' sub-claim was NOT confirmed this pass — pull the exact figure from the NCMEC/FBI primary before restoring it. Sub-claim removed from the sentence pending confirmation.

claims.claim: In the first half of 2025, online enticement and child sex trafficking reports to NCMEC continued to surge following the REPORT Act's expanded mandatory reporting.
claims.expiry: Mid-year figure; supersede with NCMEC full-year 2025 report.
red_team_flags: The specific mid-2025 figures (enticement +77% to 518,720; trafficking 62,891) were NOT confirmed this pass — pull directly from the NCMEC mid-year 2025 release before use. Sentence generalized until then.
Attribution: any surge is partly a reporting-mandate artifact (REPORT Act), not solely rising prevalence — state this.

claims.claim: Generative-AI-related child exploitation reports to NCMEC increased 1,325% in 2024 (to more than 67,000), and escalated further to 440,419 in the first half of 2025 — a fast-emerging threat category for prevention education.
claims.source: NCMEC, 2024 in Numbers; U.S. Senate Judiciary Committee testimony of L. Coffren, NCMEC (Dec 9, 2025).
claims.expiry: Fast-moving; the H1 2025 figure (440,419) will be superseded by full-year 2025 data.
red_team_flags: The H1 2025 spike is partly attributable to a handful of AI companies newly implementing detection/reporting — a reporting artifact as well as a real trend. Note both.

efficacy_evidence.title: A Systematic Review of the Education and Awareness Interventions to Prevent Online Child Sexual Abuse
efficacy_evidence.cite: Patterson et al., 2022, Journal of Child & Adolescent Trauma
efficacy_evidence.finding: Education/awareness interventions improved online-safety knowledge, though effects on risky online behavior were limited — supports prevention education while flagging its known limits.

efficacy_evidence.title: Building the Evidence on Preventing Youth Commercial Sexual Exploitation: Not a Number Program Evaluation
efficacy_evidence.cite: Jones et al., 2025, Journal of Interpersonal Violence
efficacy_evidence.finding: Youth trafficking-prevention education increased CSE awareness and help-seeking self-efficacy in a quasi-experimental high-school trial.
